title: といっても — “although I say ～ / that said”
summary: Plain form + といっても first states a claim, then qualifies it by saying the actual level is smaller or lower than the listener may imagine: “although I say ～, in fact ….” The speaker corrects a possible wrong impression.

patterns.form: 普通形 ＋ といっても、〜
patterns.gloss: plain form + といっても (できるといっても)
noun + といっても (旅行といっても)

body.p: The first clause is what people may take from the word, and the second clause tells the real situation. 料理ができるといっても、卵焼きぐらいです. With a noun or na-adjective, だ is dropped: 旅行といっても.
The second half usually shows a small amount or limited degree: ぐらい, だけ, ほど, ほんの少し. It lowers the listener's expectation.

body.h: Difference from が / けれど
body.p: Plain が or けれど only contrasts two facts. といっても specially picks out the word just said and limits its meaning. It is also used when being modest.

examples.ja: 料理（りょうり）ができるといっても、卵焼（たまごや）きぐらいです。
examples.romaji: Ryōri ga dekiru to itte mo, tamagoyaki gurai desu.
examples.tr: I say I can cook, but it's only omelets or so.

examples.ja: 庭（にわ）があるといっても、猫（ねこ）の額（ひたい）ほどの広（ひろ）さだ。
examples.romaji: Niwa ga aru to itte mo, neko no hitai hodo no hirosa da.
examples.tr: We have a garden, but it's tiny, the size of a cat's forehead.

examples.ja: 旅行（りょこう）といっても、隣（となり）の町（まち）に一泊（いっぱく）しただけだ。
examples.romaji: Ryokō to itte mo, tonari no machi ni ippaku shita dake da.
examples.tr: I call it a trip, but I only stayed one night in the next town.

pitfalls: The second half should limit or reduce the first. A sentence that strengthens it, such as 料理ができるといっても、とても上手です, is unnatural.
Do not leave だ before と with a noun: 旅行だといっても is less natural than 旅行といっても.
